2026-07-30.headline: Note: 30 Jul figures are intraday prints. A data flag first: the extract's 29 Jul row did not refresh — every field is identical to my 29 Jul AM snapshot to four decimal places and MOVE, VIX and SOFR are blank, so 29 Jul is a stale snapshot, not a close. The last fully confirmed close is 28 Jul, and all trigger tests below run off it. Score HOLDS at 25/30 — all six channels unchanged, a twelfth session at 25 — and this is the sharpest demonstration of the scale cap the monitor has produced. In twenty-four hours the war's de-escalation track was dismantled and the score did not move. The strike pause is over: after an IRGC ballistic-missile salvo at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base at Azraq in Jordan and a CENTCOM facility — five missiles, all intercepted, no casualties — the US and Saudi Arabia struck Iran-backed militias across eastern Iraq, Riyadh's first offensive combat action of the war, and CENTCOM then resumed strikes on Iranian territory on the night of 29–30 Jul, calling them 'a powerful response to yesterday's attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East.' Trump: 'They're going to get a beating.' The quiet-night count is back to zero after four. Diplomacy went backwards in the same window: Deputy FM Gharibabadi rejected Oman's 50-50 joint-management plan outright on 29 Jul, disavowed the internationally established Traffic Separation Scheme, demanded the entire inbound lane under Iranian control and said the strait 'will remain closed, and we are prepared for a restart of war.' Neither event can raise the score, because maritime and escalation have both been pinned at 5/5 since 10 and 9 Jul. The hold is an artifact of the scale, not a judgment that anything is stable. What the four market channels did is the substantive story, and it is a rates story. The FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% on a 9–3 vote — Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissenting for a 25 bp hike — and Chair Warsh, who has removed forward guidance from the statement, insisted 'There is only a target, and it is 2 percent.' The long end did not believe him. The 30Y prints 5.2060%, the first reading above 5.20% in the entire series, up 10.91 bp; the 10Y is 4.6794%, 2.94 bp back above its own 4.65% line; 2s10s has steepened 8.97 bp to +40.67 bp, the largest one-day steepening of the war; the 10Y breakeven is back above its pre-war anchor after three sessions below; and 5Y5Y forward inflation prints 2.3311% — a war high, 3.11 bp through the 2.30% upgrade trigger and only the second reading above 2.30% on record. A hold against three hike dissents, met by a bear steepener with breakevens up and the dollar down 0.51 to 100.87 on a night the US resumed bombing Iran, is the market marking down the Fed's inflation credibility rather than seeking a haven. Two lines that were disarmed yesterday are armed this morning: Stage-4 Threshold B now satisfies both legs simultaneously for the first time in the war, and US-inflation is through its trigger. Neither has a confirmed close behind it, and the two-close rule is the only thing holding the score at 25 — while yesterday's most probable next move, a Treasury 5→4 downgrade, is dead, its cushion above the 5.00% line blown out from 8.86 bp to 20.60 bp. Crude followed the news up but not far: Brent $87.72, +$2.68, still $7.28 below the $95 trigger, active COA $89.96. September hike odds have jumped to roughly 56% from 32–38%. Sequencing 25 → 25 → 25.

US STRIKES RESUMED — night of 29–30 Jul

The four-night pause (25–28 Jul), the longest of the war, is over. CENTCOM described the new strikes on Iranian territory as ‘a powerful response to yesterday’s attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East.’ Trump beforehand: ‘They’re going to get a beating’; ‘our turn.’ Quiet-night count back to zero; targets, munitions and casualties not yet released. The proximate trigger: the IRGC Aerospace Force fired ballistic missiles at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base near Azraq, Jordan, and a CENTCOM facility (28 Jul 17:45 ET / early 29 Jul local) — Jordan reported five missiles intercepted and destroyed, no fatalities; CENTCOM confirmed no casualties or damage.

Saudi Arabia enters combat — joint US–Saudi strikes in Iraq

US and Saudi aircraft struck ‘multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq’ in response to ‘over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours.’ PMF reported at least 20 killed, 32 wounded. Riyadh’s first offensive action of the war; these strikes hit Iraq, not Iran, so they were not themselves the campaign resumption.

Mediation COLLAPSED — Iran rejects the Omani plan, 29 Jul

Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi rejected Oman’s 50-50 joint-management proposal on state television: ‘If the route we have proposed is not accepted, no other formula will be accepted. The strait will remain closed, and we are prepared for a restart of war.’ Iran also disavowed the internationally established Traffic Separation Scheme and demands the inbound lane entirely under its own control, reportedly at ~$1m per ship against Malacca’s ~$70m a year in voluntary contributions. Oman is weighing a three-route alternative. No US response to the rejection itself could be found. The 28 Jul Khatam al-Anbiya bar on vessels accepting frozen-asset compensation remains in force, and the IRGC Navy said on 29 Jul it ‘targeted and stopped’ three unnamed oil tankers (Tier 3, unconfirmed).

Houthi spokesman Saree claimed a ballistic-missile hit on the Saudi-flagged tanker NCC GHAZAL on 28 Jul; UKMTO confirmed an explosion, crew safe. Further Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities and Bab al-Mandeb shipping on 29 Jul; Bab al-Mandeb ran 19 in / 18 out on 28 Jul, down 22% since the 20 Jul blockade declaration, tanker transits down 39%. Jizan refinery (400k b/d) still shut since 25 Jul; Yanbu loadings ~3.09 mb/d against ~5.16 before 19 Jul; satellite imagery suggested possible damage at Abqaiq on 27–28 Jul (unverified). Separately, drones struck two gas carriers at Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Damietta on 29 Jul — Gaslog Salem and Energos Winter (US-owned and operated) — fires on both, no casualties, attribution unconfirmed. First strike of the war on that end of the LNG chain.

analysis.intro: The US economic shock holds at 25/30 for a twelfth session while the ground under it moved more than on any day since the crisis-band crossing on 9 Jul. On the event side everything got worse: the strike pause ended, Iran fired at a US base in Jordan, Saudi Arabia joined offensive operations, CENTCOM went back into Iranian territory, and Tehran killed the only mediation framework on the table while saying it is 'prepared for a restart of war.' None of that can move the score, because maritime and escalation have been at 5/5 since 10 and 9 Jul. Readers should take the flat number as evidence that the scale has run out of room on the geopolitical side, not as evidence of stability. The four market channels are where the information is, and this morning they all point the same way for the first time in a fortnight. The FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% against three dissents for a hike, and the long end responded by repricing inflation risk rather than growth risk: the 30Y through 5.20% for the first time on record, 2s10s 9 bp steeper, the 10Y breakeven back above its pre-war anchor, 5Y5Y at a war high through its own trigger, and the dollar lower on a night of renewed strikes. Yesterday's likeliest next move was a Treasury downgrade; today the two live candidates are both upgrades, and both are one confirmed close away.
analysis.bondYieldNote: 30 Jul yields are intraday; the 29 Jul row in the extract is a stale snapshot, so the last confirmed close is 28 Jul and all trigger tests below run off it. No channel moved; score held at 25.

bondYield.title: (i) US inflation impulse — held at 4, but the trigger is through on the print.
bondYield.text: 5Y5Y forward inflation prints 2.3311% this morning: a war high, 3.11 bp above the 2.30% upgrade line, and only the second reading above 2.30% in the whole series after 2.3007% on 7 May. It is up 6.84 bp on the day and 13.16 bp on the week from 2.1995% on 23 Jul. The corroboration turned with it: the 10Y breakeven rose 7.52 bp to 2.2708%, back above its 2.2569% pre-war anchor after three consecutive closes below, so the two measures are no longer telling different stories. The mechanism is legible — a hold against three hike dissents, delivered by a Chair who has removed forward guidance and whose message is rhetorical rather than operational ('There is only a target, and it is 2 percent'; 'where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act'), against a statement that itself concedes inflation is above target 'due in part to the situation in the Middle East causing energy prices to rise.' The market read that as tolerance and demanded compensation. The discipline is unchanged and it is the whole reason the score is still 25: this is one intraday print, and the channel needs one confirmed close above 2.30% to start the clock and a second consecutive close to fire. On 14 Jul the monitor held this same channel at 3 on a 2.2061% close with a 0.6 bp margin and was vindicated; the same rule now costs a point in the other direction, which is the price of not whipsawing. If it confirms, the channel goes to 5/5 and the score to 26. The downgrade (sustained at or below the 2.142% anchor, now 18.91 bp away) is not in play.

bondYield.title: (ii) Treasury — held at 5; the downgrade that was one session away on Tuesday is now gone.
bondYield.text: The 30Y prints 5.2060%, up 10.91 bp, which widens its cushion above the 5.00% downgrade leg from 8.86 bp on the 28 Jul close to 20.60 bp — a full reversal of three consecutive sessions of approach. The MOVE leg cannot be tested at all: the series has not printed since 28 Jul (76.09), so there is no post-FOMC reading, and with the 30Y up 10.9 bp and the curve 9 bp steeper the honest treatment is that rates vol is unresolved rather than 1.09 pts from release. Both legs must clear simultaneously and sustain; neither is close now. The more important point is the character of the move. This is a bear steepener with breakevens up and the dollar down — 2Y lower 2.5 bp, 30Y higher 10.9 bp, 2s10s +8.97 bp to +40.67 bp, the largest one-day steepening of the war and a 16.4 bp retracement from the 24 Jun low of +24.25 bp. Long-duration risk premium is being rebuilt at the same time as the front end prices less near-term tightening, which is the signature of a market pricing inflation persistence rather than Fed resolve. September hike odds have moved to roughly 56% from 32–38% before the meeting. A Treasury upgrade is not available (the channel is already maxed), so this repricing shows up in the score only through Stage-4 Threshold B and through the inflation channel — which is precisely where it has gone.

bondYield.title: (iii) Oil — held at 2; the news is far worse and the price is only $2.68 better.
bondYield.text: Brent prints $87.72 intraday, a second consecutive gain, with active COA at $89.96 against Tuesday's $84.09 close. But the close-basis gap to the $95 trigger is still $12.92 measured from the last confirmed close, and $7.28 from this morning's print. That is the striking thing about this edition: the pause broke, Saudi Arabia entered the war, mediation collapsed and Iran threatened a restart, and crude added under $3. The physical picture argues for more — Jizan's 400k b/d refinery shut since 25 Jul, Yanbu loadings at ~3.09 mb/d against ~5.16 before 19 Jul, possible Abqaiq damage on 27–28 Jul, roughly 1.5 mb/d of CPC Black Sea exports still at risk, a US crude draw of 7.2 mb to 404.5 mb and refineries at 97.2% of capacity. Against it sit OPEC+ (a fifth consecutive monthly increase of 188k b/d for August, a further ~188k b/d expected at the 2 Aug meeting before a pause after September) and the IEA's remaining stock capacity (290 mb released since 11 March, over 1 bn bbl left). The two-close rule kept this channel at 2 through the $95 approach on 23 Jul and through the $12.18 unwind that followed; it stays at 2 now. The downgrade to 1 needs a mediated pause AND a close at or below $72.48 — and with Oman's framework rejected, the mediated-pause condition has moved from plausible to remote, which effectively takes the downgrade off the table even though the price leg is only $9.60 away.

bondYield.title: (iv) Political — held at 4; the pump series has stalled exactly on its line and the cross-read says it is real.
bondYield.text: AUTMUSAG has not printed since 27 Jul ($4.75), a third consecutive blank session, and per the discipline established after the JGLA episode a missing print is flagged, never carried. The useful new information is external: AAA's own published regular-grade national average went $4.099 on 28 Jul to $4.091 on 29 Jul, the first decline of the run. So the nine-session climb that ended flat exactly at $4.75 on 24–27 Jul looks like a genuine stall rather than a reporting artifact, and the channel is more likely to be held at 4 by the pump than taken to 5 by it. The DOE weekly cuts the other way (+9.5¢ to $4.096 for the week of 27 Jul), and with refineries maxed at 97.2%, gasoline stocks ~6% below the five-year average and the SPR down to ~311 mb from 415 mb in late March, a sustained crude leg higher would pass through quickly. No federal intervention — SPR release, export limit, waiver or gouging action — is confirmable in the 28–30 Jul window.

analysis.stage4Note: Stage 4 is a credit/auction event. Threshold B, disarmed on both legs yesterday, satisfies both legs on this morning’s print for the first time in the war — on an intraday basis only.

stage4.title: Threshold A · 13 May 30Y auction, cleared 5.050%.
stage4.text: Historical benchmark. The 9 Jul re-opening cleared 5.06% with a 0.3 bp stop-through. The 30Y now prints 5.2060%, 15.6 bp above the May stop and the widest margin since that auction. There is no coupon supply until the August refunding cycle, which means the next real test of long-end demand arrives with a curve that has just repriced 11 bp in a session.

stage4.title: Threshold B · 30Y above 5.20% with 10Y above 4.65% — BOTH LEGS ARMED, intraday.
stage4.text: The 30Y prints 5.2060%, 0.60 bp through its leg and the first reading above 5.20% in the series; the 10Y prints 4.6794%, 2.94 bp through its own leg, undoing the reset that two consecutive sub-4.65% closes had produced on 28–29 Jul. This is the first time in the war both legs have been satisfied simultaneously. It is not a Stage-4 event: the threshold is evaluated on confirmed closes and then on persistence, and one Singapore-morning print supplies neither. What it does mean is that B has gone from disarmed to live inside twenty-four hours, and that the mechanism now arming it is domestic monetary credibility rather than a Hormuz headline. A confirmed close on both legs tonight is the single most consequential thing that could happen to this monitor this week.

analysis.crossAsset: The cross-asset signature changed shape. For most of July the tape traded Hormuz headlines: crude, European gas and Asia LNG moved together, the dollar was inert and rates followed risk. This morning the driver is the Fed. Crude and TTF are up (Brent +$2.68, TTF +€1.53, back within €2.95 of the 24 Jul record) on the strike resumption and the collapse of the Omani framework, but the scale of those gains is modest against the scale of the news. The rates complex, by contrast, moved hard and in the specific pattern that says inflation rather than fear: 30Y +10.9 bp, 2s10s +9.0 bp, 10Y breakeven +7.5 bp back through its pre-war anchor, 5Y5Y +6.8 bp to a war high, 2Y –2.5 bp, and DXY –0.51 to 100.87 on a night when the United States resumed bombing Iran. A weaker dollar and steeper curve into renewed war is not a haven bid; it is the market charging a higher premium to hold long-dated US nominal risk. Two gaps qualify the read: MOVE and VIX have no post-FOMC print, so the volatility leg of the story is unmeasured, and equities fell into the 29 Jul close (Dow –1.4%, S&P 500 –0.5%, Nasdaq –0.5%) which the stale VIX does not reflect. Henry Hub remains 10.9% BELOW pre-war — the Hormuz/LNG-routing signature intact, this is still not a global-energy shock — while the Damietta strike on two gas carriers, one US-owned, extends the LNG-chain risk to the Mediterranean for the first time.

2026-07-30.scenarioShift: Probability shifts from the 29 Jul edition: mediated pause –15 (23→8) — the single largest one-day move in this map since the war began, and it is a collapse, not a drift; full war +12 (26→38), the highest reading of the war, on the resumption plus Iran’s own ‘prepared for a restart of war’; deal collapse +4 (20→24) on an outright rejection rather than a stall; regional relapse +1 (13→14) on the reactivated Red Sea front and Damietta; contained-but-violent –2 (18→16) because its precondition, a holding pause, is gone. watchlist: US-inflation →5 — the trigger is already through; it needs closes. 5Y5Y prints 2.3311%, 3.11 bp above the 2.30% line and a war high. One confirmed close above 2.30% starts the clock and a second consecutive close takes the channel to 5/5 and the score to 26. This is now the nearest score move and it is an upgrade. Stage-4 Threshold B — both legs armed for the first time in the war. 30Y 5.2060% (0.60 bp through) and 10Y 4.6794% (2.94 bp through), on intraday prints. A confirmed close on both, then persistence, is the most consequential single development available this week. The August refunding cycle is the next coupon-supply test and it now meets a curve that has repriced 11 bp in a session.

MOVE — the missing number. No print since 76.09 on 28 Jul, so there is no post-FOMC rates-vol reading. It matters twice: it is the second leg of the Treasury downgrade test (moot for now) and it is Threshold C. Verify it fresh in the next extract rather than inferring it.

Whether the resumption is one cycle or a new campaign — and whether Oman’s three-route alternative gets any Iranian engagement. Four quiet nights ended with a single retaliatory night. A second and third consecutive night of strikes on Iranian territory converts this from a retaliation cycle into a restarted campaign and would put full war well above 38%; a return to quiet inside 48 hours partially restores the contained-but-violent path. On the diplomatic leg, Gharibabadi’s ‘no other formula will be accepted’ closes the door rhetorically, but Al Jazeera’s sources reported some Iranian flexibility on routing before the rejection — any re-engagement is the only path back toward the mediated-pause branch, now at 8%.

Oil’s failure to price the escalation. Brent added under $3 on a day that produced a strike resumption, Saudi combat entry and the collapse of mediation. Either the market is discounting the resumption as a one-off, or OPEC+ supply and IEA stocks are absorbing more risk premium than assumed. The 2 Aug OPEC+ meeting (a further ~188k b/d expected, then a pause after September) is the test.

Political →5 — stalled at the line, and the cross-read now argues against it. AUTMUSAG has been blank for three sessions at $4.75; AAA’s published regular-grade average eased 0.8¢ between 28 and 29 Jul. Watch the backfill: a print below $4.75 would take the political channel off its trigger for the first time since 24 Jul.

Gas complex — verify the next JGLA print fresh, and watch the Mediterranean. Asia LNG has had no print for two sessions (last ¥3,418 on 28 Jul) and is never carried forward. TTF is back within €2.95 of its war record. The Damietta strike on two gas carriers, one US-owned, is the first hit on the Mediterranean end of the LNG chain and a new risk vector for both series.

methodology.scale: Six transmission channels (maritime denial, oil, US inflation impulse, Treasury stress, political stress, escalation risk), each 0–5, summed to 0–30. Bands: 0–7 watch · 8–14 stress · 15–21 systemic-risk watch · 22–30 crisis. Market channels move only on a confirmed close through a trigger; escalation-risk and maritime denial are event-based. Hysteresis note: upgrades fire on a sustained break, downgrades only on a sustained reversal past a wider threshold, deliberately, to avoid whipsawing. 2026-07-31.headline: Note: 31 Jul figures are intraday prints. A data flag first, and this time it is a resolution rather than an exception: the extract's 29 Jul row, which never refreshed for yesterday's edition, has now been fully backfilled with true closes, and MOVE, VIX, SOFR and JGLA have all printed for 29 and 30 Jul. Both 29 and 30 Jul are therefore confirmed closes and every trigger test below runs off them. Score RISES to 26/30 — the US-inflation impulse fires 4→5 on two consecutive confirmed closes of 5Y5Y forward inflation above the 2.30% trigger (2.3302% on 29 Jul, 2.3303% on 30 Jul) — the first channel move in twelve sessions and the highest reading since 12 June. This is the upgrade the monitor flagged yesterday as the nearest available move, and it fired exactly as the discipline requires: an intraday break on 30 Jul, then confirmation, and only then the point. Five of six channels are now at or above 4 and four are maxed at 5. The second consequential line also went through. Stage-4 Threshold B — the 30Y above 5.20% with the 10Y above 4.65% — was satisfied on both legs on two consecutive confirmed closes (5.2007%/4.6773% on 29 Jul, 5.2135%/4.6733% on 30 Jul), the first time in the war. The 30Y close of 5.2135% is the highest in the series and 16.35 bp above the 13 May auction stop. Persistence is now the test, and the very first print after the trigger is a shade softer: this morning the 30Y eases to 5.1965%, 0.35 bp back beneath its leg, while the 10Y at 4.6531% stays 0.31 bp above. The tape this morning is a partial give-back of the post-FOMC repricing rather than a reversal of it. Yields are lower across the curve (2Y –1.1 bp, 10Y –2.0 bp, 30Y –1.7 bp), 5Y5Y slips 0.74 bp but holds 2.29 bp above its trigger for a third session, and crude gives back $0.92 to $85.96 with the active COA at $88.18. Two of yesterday's data gaps closed and both cut against the reassuring reading: MOVE resolved at 77.09 on the 30 Jul close, up 2.91 on the day and above the 75 line that forms the second leg of the Treasury downgrade, so that downgrade is doubly dead; and Asia LNG backfilled to a rising ¥3,527, not a stale ¥3,418. The events kept deteriorating and still cannot register: CENTCOM ran a second consecutive night over Iran, describing a heavy wave against dozens of IRGC targets; an Iranian strike killed a worker in Kuwait, the first fatality on Kuwaiti soil; Jordan intercepted five more missiles; and Gharibabadi hardened again, from 'the strait will remain closed' to 'the strait will never return to its pre-war state.' Maritime and escalation have been pinned at 5/5 since 10 and 9 Jul, so none of it moves the number — the point that arrived today came from a US bond market repricing the Fed, not from Hormuz. That is the central fact of this edition and of the month now closing: July's damage was done to the long end. Sequencing 25 → 25 → 26.

A SECOND NIGHT — CENTCOM heavy wave over Iran, 29–30 Jul

CENTCOM said it struck ‘dozens of IRGC targets in Iran, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities,’ framed as a response to Iran’s 28 Jul launches. A single retaliatory night has become a two-night sequence, which is the distinction between a cycle and a restarted campaign. Iranian state media reported a family of three killed by a strike on a home on Qeshm Island and further strikes on Ahvaz (Tier 3, casualty toll not independently verified). Cumulative US losses stand at 18 service members killed and more than 600 wounded.

Iranian fire spreads — a first fatality in Kuwait

An Iranian strike hit a Chinese company’s building in northern Kuwait, killing one worker: the first death on Kuwaiti soil in the war. Jordan’s armed forces intercepted five more Iranian missiles with no casualties. The IRGC claimed an ‘Operation Nasr 2’ that destroyed drone hangars and a fuel depot at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait and three F-35s in Jordan; CENTCOM says all missiles were intercepted and the claims are uncorroborated (Tier 3).

Mediation — Iran hardens again; Pakistan says talks continue

Gharibabadi moved from ‘the strait will remain closed’ to ‘the strait will never return to its pre-war state,’ demanding total control of the northern route and calling the southern Omani corridor illegal and unsafe. The IMO confirmed it is not party to the Iran–Oman talks and that any new routeing scheme needs formal member-state submission, so neither the Omani nor the Iranian plan currently has standing. Oman’s foreign minister convened Gulf counterparts on 29 Jul. The one positive thread: Pakistan’s foreign ministry said on 31 Jul that negotiations are ongoing and that it is working to return both sides to the June ‘Islamabad MoU.’ The IRGC said two tankers attempted the southern lane on 28 Jul, one caught fire and both turned back (Tier 3, no vessel names, unverified).

Aramco has told Reuters via Industrial Info that the 400k b/d Jizan complex stays offline until mid-August after a Houthi strike damaged its IGCC powerplant and tank farm. Satellite imagery reportedly shows burn scars across four of the six spheroids at Abqaiq; Aramco has not commented, and no throughput loss is verifiable. Saudi crude has been pushed off Bab al-Mandeb almost entirely since the 20 Jul Houthi embargo, with Suez-routed volume up 106% to 1.06 mb/d and voyage times going from ~24 to ~54 days. Bab al-Mandeb ran 21 commodity transits on 29 Jul, down from 38 the day before. Saudi Arabia launched a 14-nation Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance on 30 Jul — note its remit is the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb and Gulf of Aden, NOT Hormuz. Attribution for the 29 Jul Damietta drone strike on the Gaslog Salem and the US-owned Energos Winter is still unresolved; the Houthis denied it and unnamed Iranian sources told the NYT it was designed to show what deeper disruption would look like.

analysis.intro: The US economic shock rises to 26/30, its first move in twelve sessions and its highest reading since 12 June. The point did not come from Hormuz. It came from the US bond market, which spent the two sessions after the FOMC hold pricing a permanently higher inflation compensation into the long end, and it fired only once two confirmed closes were on the board. That sequencing matters: the monitor held this channel at 4 yesterday with the trigger 3.11 bp through on an intraday print, and took the point today when 29 and 30 Jul both closed above 2.30%. The same two closes satisfied Stage-4 Threshold B on both legs for the first time in the war. Meanwhile the geopolitical track got worse again — a second consecutive night of US strikes on Iran, a first fatality in Kuwait, five more missiles over Jordan, and Iran moving from 'the strait will remain closed' to 'the strait will never return to its pre-war state' — and none of it could move the number, because maritime and escalation have been maxed since 10 and 9 Jul. This morning's tape gives a little back: yields lower across the curve, crude down $0.92, the 30Y 0.35 bp under its Stage-4 leg. That is a partial retracement of a large repricing, not a reversal, and it is exactly the kind of print the persistence test exists to absorb.
analysis.bondYieldNote: 31 Jul yields are intraday. Both the 29 and 30 Jul rows are confirmed closes — yesterday's stale-row exception has resolved — and all trigger tests run off them. One channel moved: US inflation 4→5. Score 25→26.

bondYield.title: (i) US inflation impulse — UPGRADED 4→5. The trigger is confirmed.
bondYield.text: 5Y5Y forward inflation closed at 2.3302% on 29 Jul and 2.3303% on 30 Jul, two consecutive confirmed closes above the 2.30% upgrade line, with the 30 Jul close the highest reading in the series. That is the sustained break the trigger specifies, and it is the same standard that fired this channel 3→4 on 15 Jul on the second consecutive close above 2.20%. Yesterday the monitor held at 4 with the line 3.11 bp behind it on an intraday print and said one confirmed close would start the clock and a second would fire it; both arrived. This morning's 2.3229% is 2.29 bp above the trigger for a third session, so the upgrade is not resting on a single pair of closes. The corroboration is more mixed than it was: the 10Y breakeven has come back to 2.2566%, which is its 2.2569% pre-war anchor to three decimal places, after two sessions above. That divergence is itself informative — spot ten-year compensation is unchanged from before the war while the five-year forward five-year rate is 18.09 bp higher. The market is not pricing more inflation now; it is pricing a higher terminal inflation rate, which is precisely the kind of expectations damage a central bank cannot fix with a single hike. The mechanism remains the 29 Jul hold against three dissents for a tightening, from a Chair who has removed forward guidance and whose message is rhetorical rather than operational. Note also what did not do the work: June core PCE, released 30 Jul, was +0.1% m/m and +3.3% y/y, cooler than the 0.2% consensus on the month. Breakevens rose anyway. The downgrade (5Y5Y sustained at or below the 2.142% anchor) is 18.09 bp away and not in play. At 5/5 this channel is now maxed and can only subtract from here.

bondYield.title: (ii) Treasury — held at 5; the downgrade now fails on both legs.
bondYield.text: The 30Y closed at 5.2135% on 30 Jul, the highest in the series, leaving 21.35 bp of cushion above the 5.00% downgrade leg; this morning's 5.1965% still leaves 19.65 bp. More important, the MOVE gap has closed and it closed the wrong way for the downgrade: 74.18 on the 29 Jul FOMC close, then 77.09 on 30 Jul, so rates vol is above the 75 leg, not below it. Yesterday the monitor recorded MOVE as unresolved rather than as reassurance and declined to claim it was 1.09 pts from release; that judgment holds up, though the intermediate detail is worth recording honestly — vol actually fell on decision day and only rose afterwards, so the inference that it 'has almost certainly risen' was right in net over two sessions but wrong about the FOMC session itself. The character of the move is unchanged and is the point: a bear steepener with breakevens up and the dollar down. Over July the 30Y is 26.2 bp higher, 2s10s is 12.9 bp steeper, and the dollar is 1.02 lower. This morning's small bull flattening — every tenor lower, the curve 1.0 bp flatter — is a month-end print, not a change of regime. September hike odds sit somewhere between 57% and 61% on the two independent CME FedWatch reads I can corroborate, up from 32–38% before the meeting; a 81% figure is circulating from a single non-financial outlet and is not used here.

bondYield.title: (iii) Oil — held at 2, and the striking thing is again how little crude is doing.
bondYield.text: The last confirmed close is $86.88 (30 Jul), $8.12 below the $95 upgrade trigger; this morning's $85.96 is $9.04 below it, a third consecutive lower print. Crude has now given back most of the strike-resumption bid even as the strikes ran a second night, Iran killed a worker in Kuwait and Tehran hardened its position on the strait to permanence. July was still a violent month for the barrel — +19.1% on the close basis, from $72.92 on 30 Jun to $86.88 — but the direction of travel in the last three sessions is down. The physical picture argues the other way: Jizan's 400k b/d refinery is out to mid-August, Abqaiq shows unexplained burn scars on four of six spheroids, Saudi crude has been forced off Bab al-Mandeb onto a 54-day Suez routing, and the IEA puts effective OPEC+ spare capacity at roughly 0.17 mb/d excluding shut-in Iranian and Russian barrels. Against that sit the offsets that have absorbed every escalation this month: OPEC+ is expected to approve a final +188k b/d for September at the 2 Aug meeting before pausing, and the IEA's members have released 290 mb since 11 March with over 1 bn bbl left. The US strategic cushion is the one that is visibly wearing out — the SPR fell another 3.7 mb to 307.7 mb in the week to 24 Jul, an eighteenth consecutive weekly draw and the lowest since 1983. The downgrade to 1 requires a mediated pause AND a close at or below $72.48; with Iran now saying the strait will never return to its pre-war state, the pause condition is remote and the downgrade is effectively unavailable even though the price leg is $13.48 away.

bondYield.title: (iv) Political — held at 4; the stall at the line is now four prints long.
bondYield.text: AUTMUSAG printed exactly $4.75 on 24, 27, 28 and 29 Jul and is blank for 30 and 31 Jul. The upgrade needs the series sustained ABOVE $4.75, and sitting on the line is not through it. The external cross-read continues to argue that the stall is real: AAA's separately published regular-grade national average was $4.098 on 30 Jul against $4.091 a week earlier, a gain of seven-tenths of a cent across a week in which crude traded from $82 to $88 and back. RBOB has come off its 23 Jul two-month high. The pass-through pipeline is still tight — crude stocks about 7% below the five-year average, gasoline stocks about 7% below, refinery utilisation last confirmed at 96.2% for the week to 17 Jul, the SPR at 307.7 mb — so a sustained crude leg higher would still reach the pump quickly. But it has not happened, and on the evidence the channel is more likely to be taken off its trigger by a sub-$4.75 backfill than through it. No federal intervention — SPR release, export limit, waiver or gouging action — is confirmable in the 29–31 Jul window.

analysis.stage4Note: Stage 4 is a credit/auction event. Threshold B, armed on an intraday print yesterday, is SATISFIED on confirmed closes today — the first time in the war. The persistence test now runs.

stage4.title: Threshold A · 13 May 30Y auction, cleared 5.050%.
stage4.text: Historical benchmark; the 9 Jul re-opening cleared 5.06% with a 0.3 bp stop-through. The 30 Jul close of 5.2135% is 16.35 bp above the May stop, the widest margin of the war. The supply test is now dated: Treasury publishes its quarterly marketable borrowing estimates on Monday 3 August and the refunding statement on Wednesday 5 August at 8:30am ET, with the 30Y refunding leg auctioning in the week of 10 August. The May refunding held sizes at 3Y $58bn / 10Y $42bn / 30Y $25bn and guided to unchanged coupons 'for at least the next several quarters,' with dealers not expecting increases until early 2027. Any deviation from that guidance next week meets a long end that has just repriced 26 bp in a month.

stage4.title: Threshold B · 30Y above 5.20% with 10Y above 4.65% — SATISFIED on two consecutive confirmed closes.
stage4.text: 29 Jul: 30Y 5.2007%, 10Y 4.6773%. 30 Jul: 30Y 5.2135%, 10Y 4.6733%. Both legs, both sessions. This is the first time in the war the threshold has been met on a close basis, and it is the single most consequential development in this edition after the score change itself. Two qualifications belong with it. First, the threshold is a warning that the long end is repricing in a way that historically precedes an auction or credit event; it is not itself a Stage-4 event, and Stage 4 requires the repricing to persist and then to show up in a failed or heavily tailed auction. Second, persistence is already being tested: this morning's 30Y at 5.1965% is 0.35 bp back beneath its leg, while the 10Y at 4.6531% holds 0.31 bp above. A close back under 5.20% tonight would leave B satisfied on two closes but not sustained — which is the same asymmetry the monitor applies to score channels, and the reason this is reported as a threshold met rather than a stage entered. The mechanism arming it is domestic monetary credibility, not a Hormuz headline.

stage4.title: Threshold C · MOVE above 130. Now evaluated, and far off.
stage4.text: The series resolved after two blank sessions: 74.18 on 29 Jul, 77.09 on 30 Jul. At 77.09 the index is 52.91 pts below the threshold and well under the 115.02 war high of 26 March. Recorded as far off — but note it is 3.71 above its pre-war level and above the 75 line that forms the second leg of the Treasury downgrade, so the same number that makes C remote also makes that downgrade unavailable.

analysis.crossAsset: The cross-asset signature is now unambiguous and it is domestic. Over the two sessions since the FOMC the long end repriced hard and the dollar fell: the 30Y closed at a series high 5.2135%, 2s10s steepened to +42.53 bp, 5Y5Y set a series high at 2.3303%, and DXY dropped 1.02 to 99.864 on 30 Jul, a much larger fall than yesterday's morning snapshot showed. Rates vol rose to 77.09 while equity vol collapsed to 17.09 as the S&P added 1.3% and the Nasdaq 2.3% — a split that says the stress is in duration, not in risk assets. This morning partially unwinds it: yields 1–2 bp lower across the curve, the dollar 0.30 higher, crude 0.92 lower, TTF 0.52 lower. The energy complex has been fading all week — Brent down three sessions running, TTF €5.85 off its war record, WTI back under $80 — while the rates complex did the damage. The one energy series still climbing is Asia LNG, which backfilled to ¥3,527 on 30 Jul, up ¥58 on the day and up ¥109 from the 28 Jul print that yesterday's edition had to leave hanging. Henry Hub at $2.758 remains 10.0% BELOW pre-war: the routing signature is intact and this is still not a global-energy shock. The month-end frame is the cleanest summary of July: Brent +19.1%, TTF +34.2%, the 30Y +26.2 bp, 2s10s +12.9 bp steeper, 5Y5Y +15.1 bp, and the dollar down 1.02. The war moved energy; the Fed moved the curve; and it is the curve that added the point today.

channels.name: Maritime denial
channels.rationale: Held at 5 (max). Strait closed to commercial traffic, day ~154. Traffic has ticked off the floor — Kpler 14 commodity transits on 29 Jul against single digits the prior week, Windward 20 transits of which four dark — but that is still roughly 11–15% of the 88–130/day pre-crisis baseline, and Gulf loading activity fell by more than half. Iran hardened from ‘the strait will remain closed’ to ‘the strait will never return to its pre-war state,’ and the IMO confirmed it is not party to the Oman talks, so no reopening framework has standing.
channels.downgrade: verified reopening (escorted convoys) with traffic above 25% of normal for 10 sessions → to 3–4.

channels.name: Oil price shock
channels.rationale: Held at 2. Last confirmed close $86.88 (30 Jul), $8.12 below the $95 trigger; intraday $85.96, $9.04 below it, active COA $88.18. A third consecutive lower print through a second night of US strikes on Iran, a first fatality in Kuwait and Iran declaring the closure permanent. July was +19.1% on the close basis, but the last three sessions have gone the other way: OPEC+ supply, over 1 bn bbl of IEA stock capacity and an eighteenth straight SPR draw are absorbing the risk premium.
channels.downgrade: mediated pause + close at/below the $72.48 anchor → to 1 (the pause condition is remote after Iran’s ‘never return to its pre-war state’).

channels.name: US inflation impulse
channels.rationale: UPGRADED 4→5 (max). 5Y5Y forward inflation closed at 2.3302% on 29 Jul and 2.3303% on 30 Jul — two consecutive confirmed closes above the 2.30% trigger, the second of them the highest reading in the series — and prints 2.3229% intraday today, a third session above the line. Same standard that fired 3→4 on 15 Jul. The 10Y breakeven has fallen back to 2.2566%, exactly its pre-war anchor: spot compensation is unchanged from before the war while the forward is 18.1 bp higher, which is terminal-rate damage rather than a near-term energy pass-through.
channels.downgrade: 5Y5Y sustained at/below the 2.142% pre-war anchor → to 4 (18.1 bp away).

channels.name: Treasury stress
channels.rationale: Held at 5 (max). The 30Y closed at 5.2135% on 30 Jul, the highest in the series, 21.35 bp above the 5.00% downgrade leg; 5.1965% intraday leaves 19.65 bp. The MOVE gap resolved at 74.18 (29 Jul) then 77.09 (30 Jul), ABOVE the 75 leg, so the downgrade now fails on both legs rather than one. Over July the 30Y is +26.2 bp and 2s10s +12.9 bp steeper with the dollar down — the signature of inflation-premium rebuilding, not haven demand.
channels.downgrade: 30Y close under 5.00% with MOVE under 75 sustained → to 4.

channels.name: Political stress
channels.rationale: Held at 4. AUTMUSAG printed exactly $4.75 on 24, 27, 28 and 29 Jul — four sessions ON the trigger without going through it — and is blank for 30 and 31 Jul, flagged and not carried. AAA’s published regular-grade average went $4.091 to $4.098 across the week to 30 Jul, seven-tenths of a cent, and RBOB is off its 23 Jul high. With crude and gasoline stocks each ~7% below the five-year average and the SPR at 307.7 mb there is no slack if crude runs, but it has not run.

channels.name: Escalation risk
channels.rationale: Held at 5 (max) on a day that would otherwise have forced another upgrade. CENTCOM ran a second consecutive night over Iran against ‘dozens of IRGC targets’; an Iranian strike killed a worker in Kuwait, the first fatality on Kuwaiti soil; Jordan intercepted five more missiles; Kataib Hezbollah has given Baghdad until 6 August over the US–Saudi strikes; and Iran declared the strait will never return to its pre-war state. The channel cannot register any of it.

2026-07-31.scoreTotal: CRISIS band — UP one point, the first channel move in twelve sessions and the highest reading since 12 June. The point came from the US bond market, not from Hormuz: two confirmed closes of 5Y5Y above 2.30% took the US-inflation impulse to its maximum. Four of six channels are now at 5/5. With maritime, escalation, US-inflation and Treasury all maxed, only oil (2/5) and political (4/5) retain any upside — the scale now has just four points left in it.

whatsChanged.title: 4 · What's changed since the last edition (30 Jul → 31 Jul AM)
items: Score rises to 26/30. US inflation 4→5 on two confirmed closes. Stage-4 Threshold B satisfied on closes for the first time in the war. Yesterday’s stale-row exception resolved. Source: Bloomberg unless stated.

The US-inflation impulse fires 4→5 and the score goes to 26/30. 5Y5Y forward inflation closed 2.3302% on 29 Jul and 2.3303% on 30 Jul, two consecutive confirmed closes above the 2.30% upgrade trigger, and prints 2.3229% intraday today. That is the sustained break the trigger specifies and the same standard applied on 15 Jul. It is the first channel move in twelve sessions and takes the score to its highest since 12 June. Four of the six channels are now maxed at 5/5. Source: Bloomberg.

Stage-4 Threshold B is satisfied on confirmed closes for the first time in the war. 29 Jul: 30Y 5.2007% with 10Y 4.6773%. 30 Jul: 30Y 5.2135% with 10Y 4.6733%. Both legs on both closes. The 30 Jul 30Y is the highest reading in the series and 16.35 bp above the 13 May auction stop. Persistence is the open question, and this morning the 30Y is 0.35 bp back under its leg at 5.1965% while the 10Y holds above at 4.6531%. Source: Bloomberg.

The extract’s 29 Jul row has been backfilled, and MOVE, VIX, SOFR and JGLA have all resolved. Yesterday’s data-integrity exception is closed. The 29 Jul row now carries true closes (Brent $88.09 against the stale $82.08; 30Y 5.2007%; 5Y5Y 2.3302%), and the blank series printed: MOVE 74.18 then 77.09, VIX 20.66 then 17.09, SOFR 3.65, JGLA ¥3,469 then ¥3,527. Both the 29 and 30 Jul rows are now confirmed closes and every trigger test in this edition runs off them. Source: Bloomberg extract.

Reconciliation: yesterday’s Singapore-morning snapshot ran ahead of the close on crude and behind it on the long end. My 30 Jul intraday Brent of $87.72 was $0.84 above the $86.88 close; WTI $81.67 against $80.80. The 30Y closed 0.75 bp HIGHER than my print at 5.2135%, the 2Y 2.47 bp lower at 4.2459%, 2s10s 1.86 bp steeper at +42.53 bp, and the dollar a full 1.005 lower at 99.864. 5Y5Y closed at 2.3303% against my 2.3311% print — a 0.08 bp difference, which is why the upgrade confirmed. Source: Bloomberg.

A second consecutive night of US strikes on Iran — a cycle becomes a campaign. CENTCOM said it struck ‘dozens of IRGC targets in Iran, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities.’ Iranian state media reported a family of three killed on Qeshm Island and further strikes on Ahvaz (Tier 3, unverified). An Iranian strike killed a worker in Kuwait, the first death on Kuwaiti soil in the war, and Jordan intercepted five more missiles. Source: CENTCOM / AP / Reuters / Al Jazeera / Kuwait Defence Ministry.

Iran hardened from a closed strait to a permanently changed one. Gharibabadi on 30 Jul: ‘The strait will never return to its pre-war state.’ Iran demands total control of the northern route and calls the southern Omani corridor illegal and unsafe. The IMO confirmed it is not party to the Iran–Oman talks and that any new routeing scheme requires formal member-state submission, so neither plan has standing. The counterweight: Pakistan’s foreign ministry said on 31 Jul that negotiations are ongoing and that it is working to return both sides to the June ‘Islamabad MoU.’ Source: The National / Pakistan Today / Express Tribune / IMO.

June core PCE came in cooler than expected and breakevens rose anyway. Released 30 Jul: headline −0.1% m/m and +3.7% y/y, core +0.1% m/m against a +0.2% consensus and +3.3% y/y. A cool core print did not stop the forward inflation measure closing at a series high the same day, which is the clearest evidence that this is a credibility repricing rather than a data-driven one. July CPI on 12 August is the next real test before the 15–16 September FOMC. Source: BEA via Fox Business / LSEG consensus.

Saudi Arabia launched a 14-nation maritime alliance — for the Red Sea, not Hormuz. Announced 30 Jul with headquarters in Saudi Arabia and an EU delegation attending; members include Türkiye, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt, Pakistan and Djibouti. Its remit is Bab al-Mandeb, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. It does not address the Strait of Hormuz and does nothing for the maritime-denial channel. A separate report describes a 43-nation proposal; 14 is the confirmed number. Source: Saudi Ministry of Defence via Al Jazeera / MarineLink / The National.

scenarios.name: Return to full war
scenarios.desc: Higher again and the strongest reading of the war. What was a single retaliatory night is now a two-night sequence of CENTCOM strikes on Iranian territory; Iranian fire has reached Kuwait fatally and Jordan again; and Kataib Hezbollah has set a 6 August deadline for Baghdad over the US–Saudi strikes, which is the clearest dated escalation risk on the calendar.
scenarios.path: Brent $105–140; MOVE above 90; oil to 3–4, political to 5; score 28–30.

scenarios.name: Deal collapse — talks stall on terms
scenarios.desc: Unchanged. Iran moved from rejecting Oman’s plan to declaring the strait permanently altered, and the IMO has confirmed no routeing scheme has legal standing. Pakistan’s claim that negotiations continue is the only thread and it is unconfirmed by either principal.
scenarios.path: Brent $92–108; oil to 3; 30Y sustained above 5.20% with the 10Y above 4.65%, i.e. Stage-4 B persisting; score 27–28.

scenarios.name: Contained but violent — blockaded stalemate
scenarios.desc: Lower again. This path needed the resumption to be one retaliatory cycle. It ran a second night, spread to Kuwait and drew a 14-nation regional naval response. It survives only if strikes stop inside the next 48 hours.
scenarios.path: Brent $82–92; MOVE 72–82; risk premium $10–20/bbl; score holds 26.

scenarios.name: Regional relapse — Gulf energy infrastructure hit
scenarios.desc: Higher. Jizan is confirmed out to mid-August, Abqaiq shows burn scars on four of six spheroids with no Aramco comment, Saudi crude is off Bab al-Mandeb entirely and routing 54 days via Suez, and Damietta showed reach onto the Mediterranean. Effective OPEC+ spare capacity is ~0.17 mb/d. A landed hit on the Saudi export corridor reprices everything.
scenarios.path: Brent $150+; emergency policy response; HY spreads above 500 bp; score 29–30.

scenarios.name: Mediated pause — the ceasefire sticks
scenarios.desc: Lower. Iran has moved from a tactical closure to a declared permanent change in the strait’s status, which is a harder position to walk back than a rejected fee schedule. Pakistan’s Islamabad MoU channel is the only live mechanism and neither principal has confirmed engagement.
scenarios.path: Brent $74–85; MOVE under 72; US-inflation→4, escalation→4; score falls toward 20–22.

2026-07-31.scenarioShift: Probability shifts from the 30 Jul edition: full war +3 (38→41), a new high for the map, on the second night of strikes, the first fatality in Kuwait and Kataib Hezbollah’s 6 August deadline; regional relapse +1 (14→15) on Jizan’s confirmed mid-August outage and the Abqaiq imagery; contained-but-violent −3 (16→13) because its precondition, a single retaliatory cycle, has failed; mediated pause −1 (8→7) on Iran’s move to a permanent framing, partly offset by Pakistan’s statement that talks continue; deal collapse unchanged at 24. Probabilities sum to 100.
watchlist: Does Threshold B persist? The 30Y close is the number to watch. B is satisfied on the 29 and 30 Jul closes but this morning’s 5.1965% is 0.35 bp back under the 5.20% leg. A close above 5.20% tonight makes it three of three and turns a threshold met into a threshold sustained; a close below leaves it met but not persisting. Either way the real test is dated: Treasury’s borrowing estimates on 3 August, the refunding statement on 5 August, and the 30Y refunding leg in the week of 10 August.

Whether 5Y5Y holds above 2.30% now that the channel has fired. The upgrade is confirmed and the channel is maxed, so the risk from here is one-directional. Today’s 2.3229% is the third consecutive session above the line. A sustained retreat toward the 2.142% anchor — 18.1 bp away — would be the first downgrade candidate the monitor has had in the market channels since the oil move of 3 July.

The 2 August OPEC+ meeting, and whether oil’s refusal to price the escalation survives it. A final +188k b/d for September then a pause is the expected decision. Brent has fallen three sessions running through a second night of US strikes on Iran; either the market is discounting the campaign, or OPEC+ barrels and the 290 mb of IEA releases are absorbing more risk premium than the physical picture justifies. Effective spare capacity of ~0.17 mb/d says the second reading is fragile.

6 August — Kataib Hezbollah’s deadline to the Iraqi government. The clearest dated escalation risk on the calendar. KH called retaliation for the US–Saudi strikes ‘inevitable,’ threatened US assets in Saudi Arabia specifically, and gave Baghdad until 6 August to demonstrate it can defend national sovereignty. Iraq’s PM has already cancelled his first official visit to Riyadh in protest.

AUTMUSAG’s backfill — a print below $4.75 takes political off its trigger. The scored series has printed exactly $4.75 on four sessions and is blank for 30 and 31 Jul. AAA’s published regular-grade average moved seven-tenths of a cent across the week to 30 Jul. A sub-$4.75 backfill would be the first move off the trigger since 24 July and would make a political downgrade, not an upgrade, the live question.

Asia LNG and the Mediterranean vector. JGLA resolved higher, ¥3,469 then ¥3,527, and is the one energy series still climbing while Brent and TTF fade. Verify the next print fresh; it is never carried. Attribution for the Damietta strike on the Gaslog Salem and the US-owned Energos Winter remains unresolved, with the Houthis denying it and unnamed Iranian sources telling the NYT it was a demonstration of capability.

methodology.scale: Six transmission channels (maritime denial, oil, US inflation impulse, Treasury stress, political stress, escalation risk), each 0–5, summed to 0–30. Bands: 0–7 watch · 8–14 stress · 15–21 systemic-risk watch · 22–30 crisis. Market channels move only on a confirmed close through a trigger; escalation-risk and maritime denial are event-based. Hysteresis: upgrades fire on a sustained break, downgrades only on a sustained reversal past a wider threshold, deliberately, to avoid whipsawing. This edition is the payoff to that discipline rather than a cost of it. Yesterday 5Y5Y was 3.11 bp through its upgrade trigger on an intraday print and the channel held at 4; today two consecutive confirmed closes above 2.30% take it to 5 and the score to 26. The same rule held this channel at 3 on 14 July against a 2.2061% close with a 0.6 bp margin before firing on the second close on 15 July, and spared the oil channel a whipsaw through both the $95 approach of 23 July and the $12.18 unwind that followed. Stage-4 Threshold B is evaluated identically, which is why two confirmed closes on both legs are reported here as the threshold being satisfied while a single intraday print yesterday was reported only as arming it.
